/itineraryStops/1/whyOnRoute.source_en: The strongest route for travelers who prefer relaxed pacing, photogenic backdrops, and curated café/dessert culture over UNESCO checklist completion. Walking volume is materially lower than the East route, the indoor-fallback density is good (⟦G0⟧ caves + greenhouse, O'sulloc + Innisfree), and the route works equally well on a sunny or partly-cloudy day.

/itineraryStops/1/convenience/parking.source_en: Driver-guide handles all parking; Aewol street parking is tight on weekends — private charter solves this

/itineraryStops/1/convenience/restroom.source_en: Available at all major stops; cafés have facilities for paying customers

/itineraryStops/1/description.source_en:
The most relaxed and Instagram-friendly route, anchored on Jeju's western coastline of pale sand beaches, subtropical gardens, and tea fields. **⟦G1⟧** delivers the iconic Jeju shot — turquoise shallows, white shell-fragment sand, and **Biyangdo Island** floating offshore. **⟦G2⟧** (annexed to the beach area) is a **100,000 m² horticultural park** with the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong lava caves inside its grounds and seasonal flower displays from camellia (winter) through tulips (spring) to lotus (summer). 

**O'sulloc Tea Museum, opened in 2001 by AmorePacific** on a working green-tea estate, draws design-minded visitors for its tea-plantation walks, the **Innisfree Jeju House** next door, and rotating tea-themed café menus including the famed green-tea soft-serve and roll cake. 

The day usually closes along **⟦G0⟧**, a **5 km coastal strip** lined with sea-view cafés and restaurants where afternoon and sunset hours are the local rhythm. 

The driver-guide adapts the sequence depending on tide for the beaches and on weather for the tea fields.

/itineraryStops/1/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Most stops 09:00-18:00; Aewol cafés typically 10:00-22:00 with last-order ~21:30

/itineraryStops/1/visitBasics/closed.source_en: Most stops open year-round; individual cafés close on rotating weekdays

/itineraryStops/1/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Low-to-moderate — beach walks, flat park paths, café-to-café strolls; suitable for all ages and mobility levels

/itineraryStops/1/visitBasics/admission.source_en: ⟦G0⟧ free; ⟦G1⟧ ~12,000 KRW adult; O'sulloc Tea Museum free; Aewol cafés pay-per-order. Driver-guide assists with park ticket purchase.

/itineraryStops/2/timeUsed/0.source_en: Hotel pickup and ~60-90 min transfer to the South coast (Seogwipo)

/itineraryStops/2/timeUsed/1.source_en: Morning waterfall + basalt-cliff stops (Cheonjiyeon then Jusangjeolli)

/itineraryStops/2/timeUsed/2.source_en: Lunch break in Seogwipo (Olle Market street food, or Jungmun area for sit-down meal)

/itineraryStops/2/timeUsed/3.source_en: Afternoon Sanbangsan or Yakcheonsa + market browse before return

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/0.source_en: ⟦G0⟧: 22 m single-tier waterfall with daily night illumination, 1 km flat subtropical-forest trail; Mutae eel (Natural Monument 27) habitat; admission 2,000 KRW

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/1.source_en: ⟦G0⟧: 1 km of hexagonal basalt columns up to 30-40 m tall, UNESCO Global Geopark; admission ~2,000 KRW

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/2.source_en: Sanbangsan + Yakcheonsa: 395 m trachytic lava dome + Asia's largest Buddhist temple complex; cave-temple climb to 150 m elevation; combined ~1,000-2,500 KRW

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/3.source_en: ⟦G0⟧: 620 m covered arcade, ~200 shops + ~140 vendors + 20-stall night market; signature Hallabong tangerines, black pork, octopus buns

/itineraryStops/2/smartNotes/tip.source_en: For a rainy day on Jeju, this is the strongest of the three named routes — Yakcheonsa main hall, Sanbanggulsa cave, and Olle Market covered arcade together cover ~3-4 hours of indoor time. The Sanbangsan summit itself is closed; the cave temple at 150 m is the visitor endpoint.

/itineraryStops/2/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Olle Market is the strongest single food stop on Jeju — Jeseong Bakery's octopus buns, mochi-pancakes, and Hallabong-juice stalls. The black-pork restaurants near Sanbangsan/Daejeong are also strong. Yakcheonsa's templestay vegetarian meal is bookable separately.

/itineraryStops/2/whyOnRoute.source_en: The strongest route for travelers who want geological variety in one day — a temple, a waterfall, a basalt cliff, a volcanic dome, and a traditional market all cover Jeju's signature 'volcanic island' identity. It also has the highest density of indoor-fallback options of the three routes (Yakcheonsa main hall, Olle Market covered arcade, Sanbanggulsa cave) — making it the strongest weather-flexible choice.

/itineraryStops/2/convenience/parking.source_en: Driver-guide handles all parking; Olle Market parking can be tight at weekends — private charter avoids this

/itineraryStops/2/convenience/restroom.source_en: Available at all major stops; market has multiple

/itineraryStops/2/description.source_en:
The most scenically dramatic route, weaving together Jeju's southern volcanic geology, subtropical waterfalls, and traditional market food. **⟦G2⟧** in downtown Seogwipo is a **22 m single-tier waterfall** with a 12 m wide × 20 m deep plunge pool, **illuminated daily 09:00-22:00** and reached via a 1 km flat trail through subtropical forest where camphor trees (Natural Monument 163) grow. 

**⟦G0⟧** displays a 1 km coastal stretch of hexagonal basalt columns formed by cooling lava — part of the **Jeju UNESCO Global Geopark**. **⟦G1⟧** is a **395 m trachytic lava dome formed 700,000-800,000 years ago**, with the Sanbanggulsa cave temple at 145-150 m elevation reached by a stair climb; in spring the rapeseed flower fields at the base create the iconic golden-and-volcanic-grey contrast. 

**⟦G4⟧** — at **122,100 m²** considered the largest Buddhist temple complex in East Asia, with a 30 m-tall main hall, 5 m wooden Vairocana Buddha, and 18-ton bell — sits between Daepo and Jungmun. **⟦G5⟧** is one of the few waterfalls in Asia that flows directly into the sea, while Seogwipo ⟦G3⟧ closes the day with Hallabong tangerines, black-pork specialties, and Jeseong Bakery's octopus-stuffed buns.

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Most stops 09:00-17:30. Cheonjiyeon illuminated 09:00-22:00. Olle Market: 07:00-21:00 summer, 07:00-20:00 winter; night market 18:00-24:00 daily.

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/closed.source_en: Most stops open year-round; individual market shops close on rotating weekdays

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Moderate — Cheonjiyeon trail flat 1 km, Sanbangsan stairs 0.6 mi to cave temple, market browse on flat covered arcade. Sanbangsan stairs are the bottleneck for low-mobility travelers.

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/admission.source_en: Cheonjiyeon 2,000 KRW; Jusangjeolli ~2,000 KRW; Sanbanggulsa ~1,000 KRW; Yakcheonsa free; Olle Market free entry. Driver-guide assists with tickets.
